This matches the standard pinhole camera model and is directly stated in the notes and the passage describing Equation 16.

The projection plane is tangent to the unit sphere at $\mathbf{x}_p$ [S1].

The source text explicitly states that the method projects each Gaussian onto a plane 'tangent to the unit sphere and perpendicular to this line' (where the line connects the Gaussian mean to the camera center). Geometrically, a plane defined by a normal vector $n$ passing through a point $p$ on a sphere centered at the origin, where $n=p$, is tangent to the sphere at $p$. Thus, the evidence fully supports the claim.
